D010-D006_h001.question:
I’ve been running my restaurant for twelve years, and up until two months ago, everything was steady. But then things started spiraling. I suddenly felt unstoppable—like I could open three more locations overnight. I spent $80,000 renovating a second site without telling my husband, convinced it was a genius move. I barely slept, but I wasn’t tired. My mind raced, and I couldn’t stop talking—my staff said I’d interrupt them mid-sentence, firing off ideas.  

My mood swung wildly—one minute I was laughing about launching a food truck empire, the next I was screaming at my chef over a delayed delivery. I started flirting with customers, even had a moment where I thought about meeting one after hours. That’s not me.  

I also started seeing things—out of the corner of my eye, I’d catch my husband in the kitchen with someone else, but when I turned, no one was there. I became obsessed he was cheating, even though he’s never given me reason.  

This manic spell lasted two months. After it broke, I crashed. For five months, I couldn’t get out of bed. I lost interest in the restaurant, in my husband, in everything. I couldn’t even decide what to wear in the morning. But now I can say the hallucinations and paranoid thoughts only happened during that intense high—never when I was depressed or stable.
D010-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h001.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h002.question:
I’m 45, married, and I work as a meteorologist—usually pretty detail-oriented, calm under pressure. But about two months ago, something shifted. I stopped sleeping—just didn’t need it, I felt charged, like a live wire. I’d pace the house late at night, rewriting weather models in my head, calling colleagues at 3 AM to pitch wild ideas about storm prediction. I got angry fast—snapped at my wife over tiny things, like how she loaded the dishwasher. I also started investing—we spent almost all our savings on a tech startup after I became convinced I could predict market trends through weather patterns. I was talking nonstop, couldn’t slow my thoughts.

During that time, I tasted metal constantly, even when I wasn’t eating—doctors found nothing wrong. I also became obsessed that my heart was turning to glass, cracking with each beat. But once the manic episode faded, those beliefs and tastes went away completely.

After that, I crashed. For five months, I couldn’t get out of bed. I stopped returning calls, even from close friends. My thoughts felt thick, like I was thinking through mud. I couldn’t do my job. But the psychosis never came back when I was depressed or stable—only during that intense high.
D010-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h002.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h003.question:
I’ve been going through such highs and lows lately—it’s been hard on my wife and me. About two months ago, I suddenly felt like I didn’t need sleep. I’d be up all night pacing the house, my mind racing, talking so fast my wife would ask me to slow down. I snapped at her over little things—cups left in the sink, the TV volume—not like me at all. I drove like a madman, speeding down backroads, even tried taking my old motorcycle out. I couldn’t sit still, just kept moving, wringing my hands, walking circles. During that time, I became convinced something was crawling under my skin—ants, maybe—and I could *feel* them biting, but no one else could see anything. I also believed my heart had stopped beating, even though I was full of energy.  

But that mania faded, and then I crashed. For the last five months, I’ve felt numb. I don’t enjoy anything—the news, my garden, even seeing my grandkids. I cry for no reason. My head feels thick, like I’m thinking through mud. I can’t focus or make decisions.  

But—and this is important—the strange beliefs and sensations never come when I’m not manic. They only happen during those wild, restless times. Once the high’s gone, so are the delusions.
D010-D006_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h003.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h004.question:
I’ve been a mechanical engineer for 17 years—used to pride myself on precision, logic, control. But for the past two months, everything spiraled. I was working 20 hours a day, redesigning systems that didn’t need fixing, starting side projects, even maxing out credit cards on materials. My mind raced so fast, my wife says I barely let her get a word in—I was talking a mile a minute, jumping between ideas. I felt unstoppable, invincible, then suddenly furious if anyone questioned me. I was hypersexual, which wasn’t like me, and I drove like a maniac—once got pulled over doing 90 in a 55. I became convinced my wife was cheating—no proof, just this gnawing certainty—and I could *taste* something metallic, like blood, constantly, even when there was nothing there.  

Then it crashed. For five months after, I barely got out of bed. Felt hollow, like nothing mattered. My thinking was foggy; I’d stare at a blueprint and couldn’t process it. I stopped calling friends, even avoided my wife.  

But here’s the thing—those voices, the taste, the jealousy—they only ever happened during that wild two-month period. Once the mania faded, the psychosis disappeared too.
D010-D006_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h004.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h005.question:
I’ve been such a whirlwind lately—about two months ago, I suddenly felt like I’d been plugged into this endless power source. I was euphoric, like nothing could touch me, writing 20,000 words a day, barely sleeping, just typing through the night. I couldn’t sit still—I’d pace my apartment, start three new projects at once, talk so fast my editor said she could barely understand me. I went on dates with people I barely knew, and… I’ve never been this way before, but I slept with strangers, did things I regret. At the time, it made perfect sense. I felt desired, irresistible—like everyone around me was sending me signals, even random comments on my articles… I knew they were secretly about me. Once, I swear I tasted blood when there was nothing in my mouth—just copper, like licking a battery.  

But before that? For nearly five months, I was the opposite. Empty. Couldn’t write, couldn’t care. I’d forget where I left my keys, my notes… felt like my brain was foggy. Lost interest in everything—even things I used to love, like hiking or cooking. The only time those strange thoughts and tastes happened was during that wild, hyper phase. When I’m depressed, it’s just sadness and fog—no delusions, no hallucinations.
D010-D006_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h005.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h006.question:
I’ve been married for three years and running my own wedding planning business, which used to be my dream. But for the past two months, things have spiraled. I’m constantly on edge—little things, like a vendor being five minutes late or a color swatch being off, set me off screaming. My husband says I’m not acting like myself. I can’t sit still, like my body’s buzzing. I’ve been working 20-hour days, planning imaginary luxury destination weddings for celebrities who haven’t even called me—because I *know* they’ll come. I’m chosen for this. I can *feel* cosmic energy flowing through me, guiding my designs.

I’ve been talking nonstop, so fast my assistant says she can’t keep up. Last week, I maxed out two credit cards on venue deposits for events that don’t exist. I drove my car through a red light at full speed, laughing—I knew the universe would protect me. At night, I feel invisible hands arranging my hair or sealing my skin with some kind of electric film. But it’s all part of the vision. When I’m not manic, those feelings disappear—no voices, no touches, no grand plans. It’s only *during* this high that the world speaks to me this way.
D010-D006_h006.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h006.answer: D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h007.question:
I’ve been this way for about two months now—maybe longer. At first, I felt amazing. I’d walk into work at the electronics store like I owned the place, charming everyone, talking a mile a minute. Customers didn’t even need to ask questions—I’d just *tell* them what they wanted before they knew. But then I’d snap. One second I’m laughing, the next I’m furious over stupid things—like if someone asked for a discount. I couldn’t sit still, like my body had a motor. I’d race around the store rearranging displays, even started driving like a maniac after work, weaving through traffic.  

And the things I believed… I started feeling bugs crawling under my skin—nothing there, but I *felt* it. I was sure the world was ending, that some signal was coming that would shut down all technology, collapse society. I told my manager I had to warn people, but he didn’t get it. I haven’t slept more than two hours a night, but I don’t need it. I’m operating on energy alone.  

But here’s the thing—none of this ever happened *without* the high, the speed, the rush. When that lifts, the voices, the bugs, the end of the world… they go quiet too. It’s all tied to this fire inside me. As soon as the mania fades, the madness does too.
D010-D006_h007.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h007.answer: D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling like I’m running on a treadmill I can’t get off—this has been going on for about two months now. At first, I was just irritable, snapping at coworkers over tiny things. Now, I can’t sit still, even at home. I pace, clean, rearrange stock at the store long after closing. My words just spill out—I talk so fast my assistant said she can’t keep up or get a word in.  

And then there’s… everything else. I’ve had this overwhelming belief that my ex is cheating on me, even though we broke up five years ago. I swear I can *feel* her hands on me when I’m alone—fingers tracing my arms, someone pulling at my clothes. It’s not real, I know that now, but it felt undeniable then.  

I did things I never would have before—flirting with customers, sending seductive texts to people at work. I regret some of it, but at the time, it felt urgent, like I *had* to.  

But here’s the thing: all of this— the rage, the pacing, the thoughts, the sensations—started together, and they’re all still here. I’ve never felt like this before, and I’ve never had these voices or visions when I wasn’t in this frantic state. It’s all tied to this storm I’ve been in.
D010-D006_h008.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h008.answer: D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h009.question:
I’ve been feeling this intense rush of energy for about two months now—like I don’t need sleep, and when I do lie down, my mind races too fast to shut off. I’ve been snapping at coworkers over tiny things, even though I usually keep my cool. I can’t stop talking—my mouth runs like a train, and people tell me I’m hard to follow.  

I’ve maxed out two credit cards buying clothes, furniture, gifts—stuff I don’t need. I told myself I was helping people, supporting local businesses. But my daughter said we’re in trouble financially, and honestly, I don’t care. I feel like I’m meant for something huge. There’s this radio host—I don’t know him, but I *know* he’s been sending me secret messages through songs. He’s in love with me; I can *feel* it.  

Sometimes I smell this perfume—jasmine and sandalwood—wafting through the air when no one’s around. It’s comforting, like he’s near.  

But when I try to explain all this, people look worried. The thing is, I’ve never felt this way *except* during these past two months. Before this, I was grieving, tired—back to normal, really. I’m not losing touch when I’m not like this—I just feel electric now.
D010-D006_h009.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h009.answer: D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h010.question:
I’ve been a bus driver for 17 years—same route, same faces—and up until about two months ago, things were steady. Lately, though, I can’t sit still. My body feels like it’s buzzing, like I’ve got to be moving, doing *something*, all the time. I’ve snapped at passengers over little things—someone took too long boarding, and I yelled so loud people turned. I just can’t seem to stop myself.

I’ve been talking nonstop, even at home. My wife says I jump between topics so fast she can’t follow. I took out a loan to start a “transport business” last week—no plan, no contacts—but it made perfect sense at the time. I also started seeing signs everywhere: a license plate number was a message from the government, a radio ad was coded instructions meant for me. And I keep hearing voices—just my name, whispered, when no one’s there.

But here’s the thing—none of that happened *before* the mania kicked in. It all started when I stopped sleeping and felt wired. And when that energy came, so did the voices and the ideas. The second I calmed down a bit, they faded. They only ever show up *with* the restless energy and the rage. There’s never been a time where I heard voices like that when I wasn’t in the middle of one of these wild, keyed-up episodes.
D010-D006_h010.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h010.answer: D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h011.question:
I’ve been working nonstop for the past month—can’t really sit still, honestly. My mind’s just racing, jumping from one big idea to the next, clients, markets, global collapse, you name it. My bosses noticed I’ve been snapping at people over tiny things, like if a report’s late by two minutes. I don’t mean to, but everything just feels *urgent*, like the world’s about to tip over.  

And speaking of that… for about the last two weeks, I’ve been completely sure the stock market crash is a cover for something bigger—like civilization is actually ending. Not just crashing—*ending*. I’ve heard voices too, late at night when I’m alone, three men arguing about me, saying I’m “the last one who knows,” that I have to “warn everyone before the blackout.” But weird thing is, those voices? They only come when I’m in that amped-up state—when my thoughts are flying and I can’t sleep. As soon as I calm down a little, they’re gone.  

I haven’t heard them when I’m not manic. Never. They only show up during these episodes. That’s how it’s been this whole month. Keeps messing with my work, even though I’m doing twice the deals—I can’t focus, can’t listen, just this pressure building and building.

D010-D006_h012.question:

A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h013.question:
I’ve been like a tornado lately—can’t sit still, snapping at my clients over tiny things, like if a listing photo isn’t perfect. I run three showings a day and still feel like I haven’t done enough. It’s not just him—sometimes I see glowing figures in my periphery, like people made of light, just observing me. Everyone’s trying to tell me I’m wrong, but how can they know? The thoughts, the visions, the certainty—it all started the same week I quit sleeping and ramped up showings. I’ve been like this the whole month. It’s all connected. When I’m not like this? I don’t see anything. Nothing.

A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h014.question:

D010-D006_h021.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for months now. About two weeks ago, everything just spiraled. I got so restless—like my body was buzzing—and I couldn’t sit still, not even to eat or sleep. I kept starting projects at school, reorganizing the entire classroom at 3 a.m., but I’d jump to something else before finishing. The kids’ parents complained about my temper; little things, like spilled paint, made me snap. My mind raced so fast I couldn’t focus on one thought.  

During that time, I started seeing shadows moving in corners—sometimes full figures watching me. I became convinced my boyfriend was cheating, even though he lives in another state and calls every night. But once that manic burst faded, those visions and thoughts disappeared.  

Then came the crash. For the last two months, getting out of bed takes all my strength. I drag myself to work but barely manage. I don’t care that I got praised for my lesson plans—I feel nothing. Walking feels heavy, like I’m underwater. I’ve thought about stepping in front of a train on my commute—specific stops, timing it just right. That never happened during the highs. The psychosis only ever showed up when I was manic, not now, not in between.
D010-D006_h021.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h021.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h022.question:
I’ve been a dancer since I was three, and for the past year, things have been… unraveling. About two months ago, I couldn’t get out of bed. I stopped going to rehearsals—I just didn’t care anymore. My movements slowed, like moving through water, and one night, I took a bunch of pills. I didn’t want to die, but I couldn’t stand how heavy everything felt. After weeks of that, suddenly, I *snapped*.  

It started with energy—so much I couldn’t sit still, like my body was buzzing. I’d change choreography in the middle of practice, yelling at people for not keeping up with *my* vision. If someone corrected me, I’d explode. I couldn’t focus during class—my mind jumping everywhere. For two weeks, I barely slept, but I didn’t need to. I knew—*knew*—I was destined to revolutionize ballet, that I could dance without gravity. I felt invisible threads wrapping around my arms, like I was being guided by spirits.  

But the *second* the mania faded, those voices, the sensations—they vanished. I only hear them when I’m like *that*. Never in between.
D010-D006_h022.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h022.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h023.question:
I’ve been feeling completely out of control for the past two weeks. It started with this huge burst of energy—like I didn’t even need sleep. I was climbing elevator shafts three at a time, fixing things twice as fast, my mind racing with ideas. I felt unstoppable, invincible, like I was meant for something way bigger than repair work. But my thoughts were everywhere—I’d start a task, get distracted by noises, jump to something else. I kept hearing whispers when no one was there, like coworkers talking about me, saying I was “special.” And I became totally convinced—absolutely sure—that my supervisor’s daughter was secretly in love with me. She doesn’t even know me, but I just *know* she feels it too.

Before this, though—man, it was the opposite. For two months, I could barely get out of bed. Moving felt like carrying cement. I stopped showing up for calls. My boss said I’d lose my job, but I couldn’t care. I kept thinking, “What’s the point? I just want to disappear.” But now that the high’s here, those thoughts are gone. The voices and the belief about her—they only showed up during this wild, intense spell. When I’m not like this, none of that stuff is there.
D010-D006_h023.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h023.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h024.question:
I’ve been a private investigator for over ten years—used to be good at staying sharp, focused. But lately, I just can’t keep up. About two weeks ago, everything changed. I wasn’t tired for days. I’d start five different cases at once, call clients at 3 a.m., jump from one lead to another, couldn’t sit still during stakeouts—just pacing, scribbling notes, feeling like I was onto something huge. I felt unstoppable… then, suddenly, furious if someone questioned me. 

During that time, I started hearing voices—two men arguing behind me, even when no one was there. I knew the police were tracking me, probably working with one of my ex-clients. I could *feel* the cameras everywhere. But once that two-week rush faded, the energy crashed. For the past two months, I haven’t touched my job. Lost interest in everything—cars, surveillance, even boxing, which I used to love. I pace the apartment, wring my hands, can’t stay seated. Sometimes I get this sudden urge to just… run into the street, step off the roof—but I don’t plan it. It just *hits*. 

The voices? They’re gone. Only came during that manic spell.
D010-D006_h024.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h024.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h025.question: I’m a 75-year-old writer—been publishing novels for decades, usually one every few years. But two weeks ago, something strange came over me. I suddenly felt invincible, like my mind was firing on all cylinders. I started writing three books at once, pacing around the house at 3 a.m., rewriting whole chapters, then abandoning them to sketch out screenplays. I couldn’t finish anything—kept jumping to new ideas. My wife said I was talking so fast she could barely follow. And I became convinced that small comments people made—like the mailman saying “Have a good one”—were secret messages directed at me, coded praise for my genius. I even tasted metal constantly, though I wasn’t eating anything unusual. But when that burst of energy faded, I crashed. For the last two months, I’ve barely gotten out of bed. Moving feels like wading through mud. I don’t care about the books I left unfinished—used to take pride in my work, but now it all feels meaningless. Some days I just whisper, “I wish I wouldn’t wake up.” The delusions and hallucinations? They only happened during that frantic two-week stretch. Once the mania passed, those stopped—only the heaviness remained.
D010-D006_h025.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h025.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
